issue: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account
narrative: XX/XX/XXXX To Whom It May Concern : On or about XX/XX/XXXX unauthorized charges were made to my banking account ( s ). I was alerted to this incident via the Wells Fargo electronic overdraft protection alert. I immediately called the bank that evening and then called them immediately in the morning to file the fraud complaint. The amount taken from the account in question was a total of {$2300.00}. This was also the amount of the provisional credit that was authorized for and placed in my account by Wells Fargo. An investigation ensued, and the above amount was credited within ten businesses days. After the bank contacted the merchant, I was contacted directly by the merchant via my XXXX account informing me that I had an unspecified balance due to the merchant, that needed to be remedied. I then called Wells Fargo to inform them of this email and was told to call the merchant and to get any information I could without giving any personal information. In the course of this conversation, I was advised that the account with the merchant, in my name, was opened in XXXX of XXXX and that there were transactions that transpired at that time as well. I told the person I was speaking to that I was unaware of said transactions and that I would look into it. I reviewed my online bank statements to find that there were indeed charges there and called to inform Wells Fargo of my findings. I told them that I did not authorize the XXXX transactions but was aware that those charges were past the 60-day window. I then placed all fault on myself for not realizing said transactions.The representative for Wells Fargo offered to make a new claim for those charges and said all the bank could do was deny the claims since they were past the 60 days but that I should try. During the course of time passing, the merchant returned all money for XXXX save for {$200.00} to one account and {$700.00} to another. Wells Fargo issued a final credit for the joint account to cover the non-refunded charges for XXXX. Wells Fargo had previously issued a final credit of {$740.00} for XXXX charges to make the account completely whole. In short, all charges for XXXX for both accounts have been returned to me via a refund from the merchant or from Wells Fargo. While the XXXX transactions were being concluded, the bank then stated they would credit the missing {$200.00} to my bank account. Meanwhile, Wells Fargo is indicating that they are reversing the original provisional credit minus the above {$200.00} and will be removing the new amount of {$2100.00} from my account on XX/XX/XXXX. I was told via online message and over the phone by Wells Fargo that I would receive two letters advising me of the {$200.00} credit as well as the reversal of the {$2100.00}. At the time of this writing, I have received neither letter. Moreover, the reason they stated that the reversal was occurring was that there was no liability protection for me on the immediately reported fraud in XXXX. This was due to the charges reported later that occurred in XX/XX/XXXX. The XXXX charges were added by Wells Fargo to the claim as opposed to being made into a new claim. The response from the bank was that since the charges were from the same merchant that they were forced to place them on the same complaint. I then pointed out to them that the charges appeared to be from two different places ( XXXX originating from XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX while XXXX transactions stem from XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ) . Though it is clear that this XXXX is the processing establishment or otherwise affiliated with both merchants in some way, there is no indication that these merchants are the same company. As time passed and the claim was filed, it was discovered that the merchant was the same, but that information was discovered at a later date. Once I pointed out this discrepancy of what was known at the time, the Wells Fargo agent then stated that it was the same card, so they had to be processed together. In short, the agent appeared to be determined to make sure the 60-day window was initiated in order to claim no liability for the immediately reported XXXX transactions. Furthermore, though the merchant has refunded the vast majority of the XXXX transactions, they have issued no refunds for any of the transactions occurring in XXXX at the time of this writing. As such, Wells Fargo is stating that they have no liability for the immediately reported XXXX transactions due to their adding the XXXX amounts to the original claim as opposed to opening a new claim as stated previously. I do not see why these can not be handled as two separate claims for a variety of reasons, as that is how they were reported. With that stated, I find all of these interactions with Wells Fargo to be quite curious to phrase this most charitably. I am therefore requesting documented evidence of their decision based on these regulations that were cited over the phone. These regulations were not explained and the explanations of why Wells Fargo was doing what they did have changed several times now. For example, the same vender explanation changed to the same card explanation, which later changed to it does not matter because we ( Wells Fargo ) now have the claim in this 60-day process. If it is found that that the way Wells Fargo is processing this claim is an attempt at an end around to bypass their liability to fraudulent charges, then I ask that the provisional credit continue to stay in place while this 90-day investigation ( ending sometime in early to XXXX ) is concluded via XXXX. Furthermore, I am requesting documentation which states that Wells Fargos action of adding the subsequent claim from a date prior to the initial and timely fraud claim voids the fraud protection for the first and immediately reported XXXX claim. Thank you

sub_product: General-purpose credit card or charge card
narrative: As a Bank of America customer and a taxpayer, I am extremely distressed by the bank 's new policy regarding firearms and accessories. Their actions to cut off financing and other services to legitimate, completely legal companies ( in this case firearms manufacturers producing popular and mainstream merchandise ) for political purposes sets a fantastically dangerous precedent and should be curtailed immediately. Indeed, their actions run in direct contravention to the Second Amendment of the Bill of Rights, as though Bank of America is a private company and therefore has certain rights itself, we the taxpaying people of the United States bailed out this company, and others, with hundreds of billions of dollars public money. For Bank of America and other financial companies to then turn around and not only discriminate against the very same law-abiding citizens of this country that bailed them out but to strike at the heart of our founding document and system of government at the same time is simply appaling. To add to this, there is now talk of financial institutions tracking purchases of firearms and accessories down to the customer level. For what legitimate purpose could such tracking be for, I ask? I can think of none, and truly can only see the motive as the restriction or complete denial of legal purchases paid for with one 's own money. This too is extremely dangerous, as the same logic and action could be applied to any transaction, by mistake or malice : Shop at a sporting goods store, and buy a tent, but the transaction is logged as a " firearms retailer '' - to have the transaction disallowed or your interest rate raised because you shopped at a " high risk '' store? Legally and legitimately exercise your Second Amendment rights and buy a gun - and your bank denies your next loan application as you are a " high risk '' customer? Perhaps the political winds change and another product or service is disfavored by the bank - what happens then? Shop at the wrong store, and your financial future is in jeopardy? Donate to the wrong charity and the same occurs? Go to the wrong church? Buy the wrong book? Donate to the wrong political party? What happens next? I believe that banks and other financial institutions should behave in a manner consistent with their fiduciary responsibility to their stockholders and other ownership interests, and not attempt to alienate large swaths of the country and customers based on political whim. That goes especially for such companies that were bailed out by the American taxpayer to survive their own poor business decisions. It really is a terrible joke for Bank of America to behave in such an anti-American manner. No bank or business is too big to fail - revoke their charter or break them up. I and those I know will discontinue business with Bank of America or any bank that shows such blatant disrespect for the principles that underpin our nation.

issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
narrative: Upon submitting randing requests for rates on a refi 's, XXXX XXXX from Wyndham Capital Mortgage called me. He tried to complete an application via phone during the first conversation which involved pulling my credit ( which, thank XXXX I actually asked about or he would have done it anyway ) to which I told him he was not permitted to. I told him, as I did in multiple interactions, that I knew what my score was already and that I am merely looking for the best rates and understand that if they lock me in under a certain circumstance, that may change following the actual reported credit score at the time it is pulled. I was in a rush to take advantage of the low rates and high credits being offered and was doing my best to navigate through the different lenders. While some of the prices being quoted by XXXX were among the top being solicited I was having a hard time getting definitive answers and timely answers from him. Things got so bad after 1 day that I called to complain but I couldn't get anyone to pick up the phone on the company 's main line after literally calling about 15 times. I finally just looked up the name of another rep and got word to have a manager call me. A manager never called me that day and I was panicking as I was ready to move on the rates quoted. XXXX called me and emailed me multiple times after my complaint ( even though he had failed to contact me after me trying to get answers from him for 4 -5 hours - suspicious ), although a manager still hadn't. So at this point, its getting later in the day and I knew the rates may change the next day and so I responded to one of XXXX 's emails and asked him to call me back at which point I told him we should move forward with the loan to which he replied, ... 'great, may I pull your credit score now? ' - and I said, 'yes '. Mr XXXX and I stayed on the phone while he tried to run appraisal waivers on my account and said his system was giving him an error so that he would work on it a little and then pick it up again the next day. I said, no problem as Ive gone through this process before and know that we have weeks to get all the # s and documents right. I also would have never said, " ok '' to him " picking up the process '' the next day if I didn't think we were locked into our rate as the rates could change the next day and I had been in a rush to get info and finalize the initial process. With that said, also note that on a previous day during our conversations I asked him to update me on the rates and he said that his company does not post rates twice like other companies unless something really really dramatic happens. And that their XXXX rates are applicable all day. For this reason, I did not ask XXXX to requote me when I told him that we should move forward and did not find it odd that he did not go over that again as we had discussed it multiple times in all kinds of correspondence. Come to find out the next day that XXXX had never locked us in and after sending me a text the next morning saying he was working my file, he called me to tell me rates had gone up. I said to him, yes I know that's my I '' m glad we moved forward last night. Then he told me he never locked!!!!! At that point, the credit being provided from the lender had gone down by thousands of dollars. We missed an opportunity to get the rate we had been watching very closely for a couple days and also had an illegal pull of my credit score done as the credit was only to be pulled for the loan to move forward. Since without a lock it can not move forward, the credit was pulled illegally. We tried to reason with his supervisor XXXX XXXX who finally called back after both my husband and I called XXXX to ask for him multiple times. XXXX said that because I didn't use the words, " lock me in '' it was our fault that the lock was not done. That's unfair as I am not the professional here. This company could have easily corrected this wrong from the night before and provided us the rate and credit promised, especially since if Mr. XXXX had called me the day of the incident, I would have hopefully been reassigned to another more knowledgeable and competent loan officer and avoided this situation all together. Either way, both the company and the loan officer failed in their commitment and even worse in their customer service. they also have not caused financial damage both because we have not been able to take advantage of the rates but also because they pulled my credit report under false pretenses.
